items.title: Netanyahu says Iran war 'not over,' demands uranium removal

featured_image.name: Iran must abandon enriched uranium and not produce more, Netanyahu says

items.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu declared in an interview airing Sunday on CBS's "60 Minutes" that the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran is "not over," warning that highly enriched uranium still present in Iran must be physically removed and the country's enrichment facilities dismantled before the conflict can be considered resolved.[1][2]

items.title: Hantavirus-stricken cruise ship MV Hondius docks at Tenerife

featured_image.name: Hantavirus live updates: MV Hondius arrives off the coast ...

items.description: A Dutch ornithologist's birdwatching trip to the "end of the world" has been traced as the origin of a deadly hantavirus outbreak that has killed three people and infected at least eight aboard and from the expedition cruise ship MV Hondius, which arrived off the coast of Tenerife early Sunday morning carrying more than 140 passengers and crew.

items.title: Iran's record internet blackout threatens mass layoffs as economic toll mounts

featured_image.name: Half of Iran's workforce faces unemployment risk as US-Israel war's 'hidden  target' was labor market | Fortune

items.description: Iran's economy is reeling from the combined effects of war, a record-long internet blackout, and an intensifying U.S. sanctions campaign, with mass layoffs sweeping across industries from petrochemicals to the tech sector and threatening the livelihoods of millions.

items.title: Iran sends response to US peace proposal via Pakistan after days of delay

featured_image.name: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met with Pakistan's Foreign Minister  Ishaq Dar in Islamabad on Friday as Pakistan continues diplomatic efforts  to facilitate potential US–Iran engagement.

items.description:
Iran has submitted its response to the latest US peace proposal through Pakistani mediators, Iranian state media IRNA reported on Sunday, ending days of anticipation as Washington pressed for a reply that Tehran repeatedly withheld.

The submission comes after President Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio both said last week that a response was expected imminently — only for Iran to keep Washington waiting for four consecutive days. As recently as Saturday, there was no indication that Tehran had delivered its answer, with Trump telling a French broadcaster he still expected to hear back "very soon."[1][2]

items.title: One Nation wins first federal lower house seat in Farrer by-election

featured_image.name: Farrer Byelection Campaigning Gets Into High Gear

items.description:
Pauline Hanson's One Nation party secured its first-ever seat in the Australian House of Representatives on Saturday, ending the Coalition's 77-year hold on the New South Wales electorate of Farrer in a result that reshapes the country's political landscape.

Candidate David Farley claimed an emphatic victory, leading by roughly 14,000 ballots with more than 80 percent of votes counted. His primary vote hovered around the low 40s on election night, while independent challenger Michelle Milthorpe trailed with approximately a quarter of first preferences. Liberal and National candidates each polled just above 9 percent.[1][2][3]

items.title: Global oil stockpiles draining at record pace amid Iran war

featured_image.name: Iran war is draining world's oil buffer at an unprecedented ace

items.description: More than two months after the United States and Israel launched coordinated strikes against Iran, the near-total closure of the Strait of Hormuz is draining the world's oil reserves at a record pace, sending American gasoline prices soaring and threatening European airlines with fuel rationing by summer.

items.title: Israel built secret base in Iraq during Iran war, WSJ reports

featured_image.name: Israel Built and Defended a Secret Iran War Base in Iraq - WSJ

items.description:
Israel established a clandestine military outpost in Iraq's western desert to support its air campaign against Iran and launched airstrikes against Iraqi troops who nearly discovered the site, the Wall Street Journal reported on Saturday, citing people familiar with the matter including senior U.S. officials.[1][2]

The facility was constructed shortly before Operation Roaring Lion began in late February, with the knowledge of the United States but without the approval of Iraq's government. It housed Israeli air force special forces and served as a logistical hub, positioning search-and-rescue teams closer to the Iranian battlefield, roughly 1,000 miles from Israel.[3][4][5][6]

items.title: Iran says Khamenei had minor injuries but remains out of public view

featured_image.name: Photos showing Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei

items.description:
For the first time since the war began, Iran has publicly acknowledged and detailed the injuries sustained by Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei during the February 28 US-Israeli strikes that killed his father, former Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

Mazaher Hosseini, the head of protocol in the office of the supreme leader, said on Friday that Khamenei suffered injuries to his kneecap, lower back, and was struck by a small piece of shrapnel behind his ear during the attack on the supreme leader's compound in central Tehran, according to The Wall Street Journal and Iran International. "During the attack Khamenei was not in the place where the attack took place. They hit his home where his wife was killed. He was on his way, on the stairs, when the missile struck there," Hosseini told supporters in a video shared by Nour News, a media outlet affiliated with Iran's Supreme National Security Council.[1][2][3]

Hosseini insisted the 56-year-old cleric is now "in complete health" and said his absence from public life is purely a security precaution. "The enemy is spreading all kinds of rumours and false claims. They want to see him and find him, but people should be patient and not rush. He will speak to you when the time is right," he added.[2][1]

items.title: UK sends warship to Hormuz as Iran rebuffs US deadline on peace deal

featured_image.name: HMS Dragon heads to Middle East as UK considers international Strait of  Hormuz operation

items.description: The fragile month-long ceasefire between the United States and Iran faces its most serious test yet, with military clashes in the Strait of Hormuz escalating even as Washington awaits Tehran's response to a new peace proposal that could set the stage for ending the conflict.

items.title: Russian drone kills civilian hours into US-brokered ceasefire

featured_image.name: Ukraine, Russia Confirm US-Brokered Three-Day Truce, ...

items.description:
A Russian FPV drone struck a civilian car in the Polohy district of Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia Oblast on Saturday, May 9, killing a 67-year-old driver on the spot and injuring two passengers — hours into a US-brokered three-day ceasefire meant to pause all fighting between Russia and Ukraine.[1][2][3]

The attack underscored the fragility of the truce even as Moscow held its annual Victory Day parade on Red Square, an event that had been scaled back amid security concerns over potential Ukrainian strikes.[4]

items.title: WHO chief arrives in Spain ahead of hantavirus ship docking

featured_image.name: WHO chief arrives in Spain before hantavirus-hit ship evacuation

items.description:
The MV Hondius, a Dutch-flagged expedition cruise ship at the center of a hantavirus outbreak that has killed three people, is expected to arrive in Tenerife in Spain's Canary Islands early Sunday morning, as WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus traveled to Spain on Saturday to personally oversee the disembarkation of more than 140 passengers and crew.[1][2][3]

"This is not another Covid," Tedros told residents of Tenerife, emphasizing that no one aboard the ship is currently showing symptoms and that "the risk for the population of Canary Islands and globally remains low."[4][3]

items.title: US restates opposition to West Bank annexation at UN

featured_image.name: US opposes Israeli annexation of West Bank, diplomat tells UN

items.description:
A U.S. diplomat told the United Nations on Friday that Washington opposes Israeli annexation of the occupied West Bank, restating a position the Trump administration has maintained since taking office amid growing alarm over settlement expansion and escalating violence against Palestinians.

Ambassador Jeff Bartos, the U.S. representative for U.N. Management and Reform, delivered the message during an Arria-formula session convened by the Security Council's five European members — Denmark, France, Greece, Latvia, and the United Kingdom — to hear testimony on conditions facing Palestinians in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem.[1][2]

"As President Trump has made clear, the United States opposes Israeli annexation of the West Bank," Bartos said. "Stability in the West Bank is vital for Israel's security and aligns with our goal of achieving peace in the region."[1]

items.title: US sanctions Chinese satellite firms over Iran war

featured_image.name: How Chinese satellites have boosted Iran's war effort

items.description: The United States on Friday imposed sanctions on three Chinese companies accused of supplying satellite imagery that enabled Iranian military strikes against American forces in the Middle East, a move that adds a layer of tension just days before President Donald Trump is set to visit Beijing for a summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping.

items.title: Israel to release two Gaza flotilla activists for deportation

featured_image.name: UN demands Israel release Gaza flotilla activists, investigate abuse claims

items.description: Two activists detained after Israeli forces intercepted the Gaza-bound Global Sumud Flotilla last month are being released from Israeli security detention on Saturday and will be deported in the coming days, according to their legal representatives and the human rights organization Adalah.[1][2]

items.title: Bahrain arrests 41 over alleged links to Iran's IRGC

featured_image.name: Bahrain Says it Has Arrested 41 People Linked to IRGC

items.description: Bahrain's Interior Ministry announced on Saturday the arrest of 41 individuals it described as members of a network linked to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, escalating a security crackdown that human rights groups say has disproportionately targeted the country's Shia Muslim population since the outbreak of war in the region.

items.title: US intel says Iran's Khamenei shaping war strategy

featured_image.name: What to know about Ali Khamenei, Iran's supreme leader

items.description: Iran's new Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei is playing a key role in shaping Tehran's war strategy and negotiations with the United States despite remaining out of public view for more than two months, according to a U.S. intelligence assessment reported by CNN on Thursday. The assessment comes as Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian confirmed he recently met with Khamenei in person, easing weeks of speculation about whether the wounded leader was capable of governing.[1]

items.title: Trump announces three-day Russia-Ukraine ceasefire with prisoner swap

featured_image.name: Trump announces 3-day ceasefire in Russia-Ukraine war

items.description: President Donald Trump announced on Thursday a three-day ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine, declaring on Truth Social that the pause will include a suspension of all kinetic activity and a prisoner exchange of 1,000 individuals from each country. The announcement came as both sides were already trading accusations of violating earlier, competing unilateral truces declared in the lead-up to Russia's Victory Day celebrations on May 9.[1][2]

items.title: Rubio calls Iran's claim over Strait of Hormuz 'unacceptable' as U.S. awaits deal response

featured_image.name: Impostor uses AI to impersonate Rubio and contact foreign and U.S.  officials : NPR

items.description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio declared on Friday that Iran's effort to assert control over the Strait of Hormuz was "unacceptable," warning from Rome that the international community must be prepared to respond with "more than strongly worded statements" to push back against Tehran's claims over the critical waterway.[1][2][3]

items.title: Iran's FM says missile arsenal grew despite US strikes

featured_image.name: Iran's Missile Arsenal in the 2026 Conflict

items.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Friday dismissed a U.S. intelligence assessment that Iran's missile capabilities had been degraded by months of American and Israeli strikes, claiming Tehran's arsenal has actually grown since the war began and declaring Iran "1,000% ready" to defend itself.

items.title: Satellite images reveal massive oil spill near Iran's Kharg Island

featured_image.name: Massive oil slicks spotted off Iran's Kharg Island as Trump touts Hormuz  clash

items.description: Satellite imagery has revealed a large oil spill spreading across dozens of square kilometers of sea near Iran's Kharg Island, the country's primary crude export terminal, as the U.S. naval blockade continues to choke Tehran's oil trade and push its storage capacity toward its limits.
